answer: Each agent must lock a nontransferable bond before bidding, then complete a randomly assigned task that other agents can verify to reclaim it. At the summit, a jade trader could create many identities, but each needs separate capital and risks losing its bond if it fails or duplicates work. A Sybil attack therefore ties up funds across identities and exposes them to forfeiture, while an honest agent needs only one bond. A shared identity cannot reuse the same locked stake at the wharf.
